text:
alex_cheng: quick thread — Customer:AtlasPay wants a tighter 95th p99 latency SLO for short-chat flows (<=64 tokens). Their current SLA requires 80ms p95 but they asked for 50ms. This collides with our KV prefetch policy which increases batching headroom. can we scope a PRD + RFC to map tradeoffs and minimum launch criteria?
maria_gonzalez: noted. are they expecting this on Hosted or Dedicated? that changes acceptable latency/cost tradeoffs.
alex_cheng: Hosted first, with Dedicated followup. they want a clear migration path and fallback behavior if prefetch/kv misses spike.
samir_patel: high level: we can tune prefetch aggressiveness + smaller batch windows for short flows, but cost will go up and throughput drops. need acceptance criteria: p95/p99 targets, cost delta threshold, and rollback triggers.
zoe_lin: can we also include kernel-selection fallback as a safety? e.g., fall back to lightweight attention kernel for short sequences when KV miss rate > X% to avoid jitter.
ops-bot: @channel NEW-REQ: atlaspay latency ask logged -> PROD-REQ-823. Please attach RFC by EOW.
maria_gonzalez: draft PRD outline suggestion:
- Problem statement (customer ask and constraints)
- Success metrics (p95 <= 50ms for <=64 tokens; p99 <= 120ms; cost delta < 20%)
- Technical approaches (1) aggressive prefetch heuristics, (2) dynamic batching window reduction for short flows, (3) attention-kernel fast-path fallback, (4) KV TTL tuning + eviction policy adjustments
- Acceptance criteria & launch gating (synthetic qps test, canary in Hosted region with 10% traffic, latency heatmaps, rollback thresholds)
- Edge cases (cold start, tail events, autoscaling spikes, fairness across tenants)
- Owner + timeline
I can draft this today if someone owns the RFC.
alex_cheng: assign RFC owner: @samir_patel to lead RFC + perf evals. @zoe_lin to draft kernel fallback spec. @maria_gonzalez to own PRD and acceptance criteria. I'll be PM reviewer.
samir_patel: ack. I'll start with perf matrix: short flow = seq<=64, weight downsampled traces, simulate kv_miss_rate [0..50%], batch window 0-10ms, prefetch thresholds [3,8,16 tokens]. quick snippet of the perf job config I'm going to run:```yaml
job: short_flow_latency_eval
seq_len: 64
batch_window_ms: [0,2,5,10]
prefetch_tokens: [0,3,8,16]
kv_miss_rate: [0.0,0.05,0.1,0.2,0.5]
metrics: [p50,p95,p99,cost_per_1k_tokens]
```
samir_patel: question for runtime folks: what are the current safe defaults for eviction and KV TTL on hosted? we don't want aggressive TTL to cause cache churn for other tenants.
zoe_lin: current default TTL is 60s with LRU shard-level eviction. Kernel fallback: propose a deterministic selector: if seq_len<=64 && kv_miss_rate>0.15 && observed_p95_delta>25ms -> switch to attn-fast kernel for next N requests. need to specify hysteresis counters to avoid flip-flop.
maria_gonzalez: good. acceptance gating I'm proposing:
- Synthetic perf: p95<=55ms across 3 runs at target qps with kv_miss<=10% (to allow leeway)
- Canary: 10% traffic, 48h, monitor p95/p99, error rate, cost delta; rollback if p99 increases >20% or error_rate >0.5%
- Ops playbook: explicit steps for disable prefetch, disable kernel fallback, and revert launch flags
alex_cheng: edge-case note: bursty traffic where prefetch unintentionally increases prefetch pressure and bumps other customers' latency. include tenant isolation SLOs and guardrails (rate caps per customer).
samir_patel: will include perf results and cost modeling in RFC. also need to enumerate instrumentation points: kv_miss_rate per route, kernel-switch reasons, latency histograms, batch sizes.
zoe_lin: I'll write fallback pseudocode and the hysteresis counters. initial idea:
```python
def choose_kernel(seq_len, kv_miss, p95_delta):
    if seq_len>64: return 'attn-opt'
    if kv_miss>0.15 and p95_delta>25:
        counter += 1
    else:
        counter = max(counter-1,0)
    if counter>=3:
        return 'attn-fast'
    return 'attn-opt'
```
zoe_lin: also propose an opt-in rollout flag per customer so AtlasPay can request it in Hosted without affecting others.
maria_gonzalez: timeline: PRD by tomorrow noon, RFC draft by Thu EOD, perf runs Wed night, canary planned next week if perf looks good.
ops-bot: REMINDER: create canary env with tag=atlaspay-prefetch-test and enable detailed tracing.
alex_cheng: thanks all — @samir_patel start RFC and paste link here when ready. I'll set up a short sync Thu 11am to review acceptance criteria and rollback plan. :thumbsup:
